newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks in last-minute recovery on Dow Jones.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks in last-minute recovery on Dow Jones.

text.p: Mexican stocks recovered in the final minutes of dealing from a dull session to close slightly ahead on Friday, driven by strong gains on Wall Street and foreign buyers, traders said.
"The Dow enhancing its gains had its effect and some foreigners also stepped into the market. I wouldn't rule out their giving it a little shove at the close," a trader said.
"Everyone was worried that the IPC was below 3,750 points," he added.
The leading IPC share index ended up 8.27 points, or 0.22 percent, at 3,764.88.
The Dow Jones meanwhile closed up 94.72 points at 7,071.20.
The IPC was in the doldrums for most of the session, and had earlier fallen to a low of 3,737.32 in what traders said was a dull day.
Many in Mexico were on vacation Friday to take advantage of public holidays for Labor Day on Thursday and another on Monday to commemorate the battle of Puebla.
Analyst Roberto Galvan of the Bursametrica consultancy said the downward trend was due to stocks lining up with Mexican ADRs after Thursday's holiday.
"It slid in line with yesterday's decline in ADRs. Nonetheless, it is still generally moving sideways, with little volume and just quick in-and-out dealing," he said.
"Furthermore, many investors acquired positions earlier in the week in order to go on vacation," he added.
On the broad market, 104 stocks traded, of which gainers outnumbered sliders by 48 to 31.
Soft drinks bottler Embotelladoras del Valle de Anahuac headed the prominent gainers' list .PG.MX, up 26 centavos to 5.56 pesos on what several dealers said were favorable first quarter earnings.
